correctness_confidence.basis: All 16 core theorems are verified in zero-dependency Lean 4 v4.35.0 with 0 sorry and 0 warnings, and 9/9 exact-Q certificates pass verification without floating-point errors.

novelty.basis: Introduces zero-enumeration dual certificates and signed frustration atoms that bypass the 2^{\Theta(n^2)} stabilizer polytope wall for multi-qubit magic quantification.

reproducibility.basis: Complete artifact suite with deterministic Python execution, exact-Q arithmetic, and Lean 4 formal proofs provided under an open-source license.

rigor.basis: Rigorous algebraic foundations combining symplectic dual atoms, Chvátal-Gomory integer-floor rounding, and an extensive 28-attack adversarial test suite.

significance.basis: Enables polynomial-time mixed-state magic certification up to 32+ qubits, resolving open problems in W-state marginals and worst-case random access codes.

potential_errors: Assumes physical realizability of input expectations externally when derived via experimental tomography or analytical ansatz.
strengths: Formal machine-checked Lean 4 verification of all 16 core theorems
Exact-Q verification bypassing super-exponential stabilizer polytope enumeration
Robust adversarial suite rejecting 28/28 malformed or forged inputs
Innovative three-tier hierarchy separating clique covers and signed frustration atoms
strong_novelty_candidates: Zero-enumeration symplectic dual certificates for mixed-state Robustness of Magic
Signed frustrated commuting-triple atoms for enhanced stabilizer ceiling bounds
summary: The paper presents a rigorous, machine-checked framework for zero-enumeration exact-Q certification of multi-qubit quantum mixed-state Robustness of Magic using symplectic anticommuting cliques, Chvátal-Gomory integer-floor rounding, and signed frustrated commuting triples. All 16 core theorems are mechanized in Lean 4 with zero apologies, and 9 certificates up to 32 qubits are validated.
weaknesses: Requires pre-supplied atom decompositions or state expectations rather than solving the global optimization problem autonomously
Assumes global PSD quantum-state realizability of supplied expectation values
